stories.headline: Is the Rules-Based International Order Dead? The world is undergoing what might be the greatest geopolitical transformation since the end of World War II.
stories.summary: The world is undergoing a significant geopolitical transformation, potentially the greatest since World War II. Analysts suggest that US actions have ended the post-World War II order, although its applicability to the Global South is unclear. Germany's chancellor and Canada's Prime Minister have stated that the international rules-based order is no longer in effect. The US secretary of state has responded, referencing the Trump administration's stance. The order was never fully accepted by countries like Iran and Russia, which follow different ideologies. The 20th-century international order, built on post-WWII institutions, is fraying due to systemic shifts, including the weaponization of various domains. This transformation has led to a reevaluation of the global power structure and the rules that govern international relations. The future of the international order remains uncertain.

stories.headline: Europe heatwave live: UK temperatures forecast to reach 38C; French PM to hold crisis meeting after heat deaths Temperatures could smash June record in England and Wales set in 1976; red alerts in France after 19 heat deaths
stories.summary: A severe heatwave is gripping Europe, with the UK forecast to reach 38C (100F) this week, potentially smashing the June record set in 1976. A four-day amber weather warning is in effect, with "tropical night" temperatures expected. In France, 19 heat-related deaths have been reported, prompting the Prime Minister to hold a crisis meeting. Red alerts have been issued in France, with alcohol bans in affected areas. Much of Europe is enduring extreme heat, with temperatures soaring toward record levels. Authorities are taking measures such as closing schools and canceling public events to mitigate the effects of the heatwave. The UN Secretary General has described London as "cooking" due to the extreme temperatures, highlighting the severity of the situation. The heatwave is expected to continue throughout the week, with record temperatures forecast.

stories.headline: UK economy and politics in charts Ten years after the Brexit vote, CNBC compiled these charts show how the U.K. has changed across growth, immigration, sterling, trade and politics.
stories.summary: The UK economy has failed to experience a post-Brexit boost after ending ties with its largest trading partner, the EU. Ten years after the Brexit vote, the country's economic performance shows severe costs for households and businesses. Brexit is estimated to have reduced the UK's GDP by 6-8% by 2025, according to Stanford professor Nicholas Bloom. The coronavirus pandemic and Russia's invasion of Ukraine also hit global growth, but Brexit has acted as a persistent drag on the UK economy, compounding deep-seated structural problems. Key issues during the Brexit campaign, including immigration, trade, and the economy, have been significantly impacted. The 10th anniversary of the Brexit vote marks a clear verdict on Britain's economic performance, with the UK leaving the EU in January 2020 after fraught negotiations. Charts compiled by CNBC illustrate the changes across growth, immigration, sterling, trade, and politics.

stories.headline: Powerful sedative found in illicit vapes Health authorities are warning the sedative effect could be deadly if mixed with alcohol and other drugs.
stories.summary: A potent sedative called etomidate has been found in illicit vape products sold in Australia, prompting health authorities to issue a warning. Etomidate is a powerful anaesthetic that can cause rapid-onset sedation, confusion, vomiting, and loss of consciousness. The sedative effect can be deadly if mixed with alcohol and other drugs. Illicit vape pods containing etomidate have been linked to a growing number of acute drug harm cases nationwide. The substance has been detected in vape products sold under names like space oil, k-pods, and space vapes. One in three seized vapes contained etomidate, leading the Ministry of Health to work with the Ministry of Home Affairs to address the issue. The discovery represents a serious public health threat, combining the addictive potential of vaping with the dangerous effects of a potent anesthetic drug.

stories.headline: Valve is one of the few companies that has clearly explained why high tech prices are happening.
stories.summary: Valve has explained the reason behind the high prices of its Steam Machine, citing the significant investments in generative AI technology and the resulting huge demand for components. The company had initially expected PC hardware prices to decrease over time, but the component crisis forced a reconsideration of its pricing plans. Rising RAM and storage costs made the original pricing goal impossible, limiting launch availability. Unlike some companies, Valve is not subsidizing the hardware, contributing to the high prices. The company had started sourcing parts for the Steam Machine in 2023, but the unexpected cost increases led to a change in plans. The high demand for components, driven by the need for data centers to power generative AI technology at scale, has led to a surge in prices, affecting the pricing and availability of the Steam Machine.

stories.headline: Sophia Space, Inc., a leader in space-based edge computing, today announced it has selected Apex, the
stories.summary: Sophia Space, Inc., a leader in space-based edge computing, has selected Apex as the supplier of a satellite bus for a demo mission. The mission will utilize Apex's Nova bus platform to bring real-time orbital computing to enterprise, government, and defense customers. The demonstration mission is scheduled for 2027 and will showcase Sophia Space's TILE (Thermal Integrated LEO Edge) compute modules for real-time orbital processing. Sophia Space has raised $10 million from investors, including Alpha Funds and Unlock Venture Partners. The company plans to test a new approach to passively cooling space computers on the ground before launching the satellite demo by late 2027 or early 2028, proving the effectiveness of its technology in orbit. This partnership and funding will enable Sophia Space to advance its space-based edge computing capabilities.

stories.headline: Huawei today launched a new enterprise smartwatch - Qingyun H3550 with significant health and fitness upgrades.
stories.summary: Huawei has launched the Qingyun H3550, a new enterprise smartwatch with significant health and fitness upgrades. The commercial wearable bears a resemblance to the Apple Watch series but boasts distinct internal specifications and capabilities. As a latest addition to Huawei's smartwatch lineup, the Qingyun H3550 joins other notable models such as the Watch 5, Fit 4 Pro, GT 5 Pro, and Watch D2, all of which are known for their health, fitness, and outdoor tracking features. The Qingyun H3550 is designed for enterprise use, suggesting it may offer specialized features for business or organizational settings. Huawei continues to expand its range of smartwatches, catering to various needs and preferences. The launch of the Qingyun H3550 underscores the company's commitment to innovation in the wearable technology sector. Further details on the smartwatch's specifications and pricing are expected to be released.

stories.headline: Researchers at Nanyang Technological University, Singapore, have developed a label-free imaging strategy that maps subcellular dynamics in living
stories.summary: Researchers at Nanyang Technological University, Singapore, have developed a label-free imaging strategy using wide-field interferometric scattering (iSCAT) microscopy. This optical technique has nanometer-scale sensitivity and maps subcellular dynamics in living cells. The study, published in PhotoniX Life, utilizes statistical analysis of stochastic fluctuations in iSCAT image sequences to provide an intrinsic marker of cellular states and mechanical properties. This breakthrough has potential applications in mechanobiology, cancer diagnostics, and stem cell therapies. Additionally, the university has announced another advance, known as Limited-Size Object Microscopy (LSOM), which enables label-free super-resolution imaging of isolated nano-objects. By combining principles of Image Scanning Microscopy with interferometric detection, this technique pushes the boundaries of spatial resolution, contrast, and sensitivity in label-free microscopy, transforming how researchers observe nanoscale structures. These developments promise to significantly impact various fields of research.

stories.headline: Lionel Messi Sends Clear Message After Argentina's Tough Win Against Austria
stories.summary: Lionel Messi led Argentina to a 2-0 win over Austria at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, on Monday, securing a spot in the 2026 World Cup Round of 32. Messi scored twice, becoming the all-time leading scorer in men's World Cup history. His brace propelled Argentina into the knockout stage. After the match, Messi emphasized that Argentina will always fight for a win, regardless of the opponent. The victory marked a significant milestone for Messi, who broke the World Cup goals record. The win was a testament to Argentina's determination, with Messi's performance being the decisive factor. With this win, Argentina advances to the next round, while Messi solidifies his position as the top scorer in men's World Cup history. The match was played in front of a crowd at the Dallas Stadium, with Messi's goals being the highlight of the game.

stories.headline: Tottenham may offer 3 players in Tonali transfer swap as Newcastle star makes feelings clear
stories.summary: Tottenham Hotspur is pursuing Newcastle United midfielder Sandro Tonali, with the player reportedly keen on joining the North London side. Tonali wants to explore his options this summer, making his feelings clear about a possible move away from St James' Park. Newcastle is demanding a sizeable sum for the player, but Spurs could meet the valuation by offering players in a swap deal. Three Tottenham players could potentially be included in the deal to help land Tonali. Fabrizio Romano revealed Tonali's stance on a Tottenham move, citing an "important detail." Despite Newcastle's demands, Spurs are getting serious about signing Tonali, with the player open to a move to the club. Tottenham has been one of the busiest teams in the transfer market, and signing Tonali would be a significant addition to their squad.

stories.headline: Liverpool next transfer priority is obvious with deal for 'revelation' already wrapped up
stories.summary: Liverpool has already made summer signings, including Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz, but sporting director Richard Hughes is expected to make more transfers. The club has rejected Inter's second bid for Curtis Jones, and former player Stan Collymore believes another position should be the priority. Meanwhile, Liverpool is still pursuing Alexander Isak to strengthen their strikeline before the transfer window closes. The Reds have been active in the summer transfer window, with more signings anticipated in the coming weeks. Richard Hughes is leading the transfer efforts, aiming to bolster the team's lineup, particularly in the striker position, with Isak being a key target. Liverpool's transfer business is ongoing, with the club looking to finalize more deals before the window closes.

stories.headline: Kerry entered last weekend as Sam Maguire contenders. They came away as outright favourites
stories.summary: Kerry has emerged as the outright favourite to win the All-Ireland Senior Football Championship after a strong performance last weekend. They are bidding to lift the title for a record-extending 40th time. The team's attack has been impressive, laying waste to the 2024 All-Ireland champions for the second year running. With Armagh and Donegal out of the running, Kerry's chances have improved significantly. Dublin's victory over Donegal has also contributed to Kerry's favourable position. Bookmakers, such as Paddy Power, have priced Kerry as the favourite to win the championship. The team's dominance in the middle of the field was a key factor in their Sam Maguire success last year, and they will look to reestablish this dominance in upcoming matches. Kerry's strong club performances over the winter have also contributed to their favourable position.

stories.headline: Devastating building fire in Lucknow brings development authority’s actions under scrutiny
stories.summary: A devastating fire in Lucknow's Aliganj area claimed 15 lives, mostly students, and left several others injured. The building where the fire occurred had a history of unauthorized construction, with a demolition order issued in 2016 that was later revoked within two months. Following the tragedy, the development authority's past records and actions regarding the building have come under scrutiny. Investigators have found that the building had previously faced action over alleged construction violations. Authorities are now examining the regulatory actions taken and the building's history to determine if any lapses contributed to the tragedy. The fire has raised questions about the effectiveness of the development authority's oversight and enforcement of building codes and regulations in the area. An investigation into the cause of the fire and the building's history is ongoing.

stories.headline: Minister George Kurian resigns as BJP skips him for Rajya Sabha term
stories.summary: Veteran BJP leader George Kurian resigned as a Union Minister after his six-year term in the Rajya Sabha expired on June 21. The party did not renominate him to the Upper House of Parliament, prompting his resignation from the Union Council of Ministers on June 23. Kurian, a senior BJP leader since its inception in 1980, has also practiced as an Advocate at the Supreme Court of India. His resignation was necessitated by the expiry of his Rajya Sabha term, as per parliamentary rules. Kurian had credited his elevation as a Union Minister to Narendra Modi, highlighting his appreciation for the opportunity to serve. With his term ending and no renomination, Kurian stepped down from his ministerial position, marking the end of his current tenure in the government.

stories.headline: 'Mocked as actor's party': Tamil Nadu CM Vijay's 'reel' to real speech in assembly; Karur stampede, CAA in focus
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay addressed the state assembly, dismissing claims that he transitioned directly from cinema to politics as a "reel" narrative. He highlighted his party, Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam's (TVK), years of activism and public engagement, which led to its rise to power. Vijay recalled TVK's opposition to the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA) and mentioned the Karur stampede controversy. He pushed back against critics who labeled TVK as merely an "actor's party," citing decades of public welfare work. The TVK emerged as the single-largest party in the Tamil Nadu Assembly after the April-May election and formed the government with support from former DMK allies. Vijay's speech aimed to establish his party's credibility and refute criticisms of its legitimacy. The address covered various issues, showcasing the party's commitment to public service and governance.

stories.headline: Tamil Nadu Moves Supreme Court Against Deepa Thoon Lamp Lighting
stories.summary: The Tamil Nadu government has approached the Supreme Court against a Madras High Court order permitting the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepa Thoon in Thiruparankundram Hill. The Madras High Court had allowed the traditional lighting of the lamp, providing relief to Hindu devotees. However, the state government has challenged this decision, filing a petition with the Supreme Court. The key issue is not a ban on lighting the Karthigai Deepam, but rather the demand for the lamp to be lit at a specific location. The Supreme Court will hear the government's appeal, considering the matter further. The move comes after the Madras High Court's order was seen as a significant development in the Karthigai Deepam row, which has been a point of contention. The Supreme Court's decision is now awaited.

stories.headline: Russian oil is flowing into India—but what about the geopolitical angle?
stories.summary: Russia's share of India's crude oil imports has significantly increased, reaching 21.6% in 2022-23, 35.9% in 2023-24, and 35.8% in 2024-25. Despite international criticism and sanctions, India continues to purchase Russian oil, driven by economic and strategic factors. The US has provided a temporary waiver for India's Russian oil imports, but uncertainty remains over whether it will be extended. Indian leaders have cited the need for cheap energy to support the country's large and impoverished population. The imports are expected to continue, with inward shipments poised to hit new highs. India's diplomacy has played a key role in navigating the situation, with the country seeking to balance its relationships with major powers while meeting its energy needs. The US waiver has provided a temporary reprieve, but India's long-term strategy remains to be seen.

stories.headline: Iran Deal Back On Track? Trump, Tehran Agree To 60
stories.summary: The United States and Iran have agreed to a 60-day roadmap to reach a final agreement, following nearly 18 hours of talks in Switzerland. A preliminary 14-point memorandum of understanding has been revealed, outlining key commitments from both sides. The US will immediately lift its blockade and waive Iranian oil sanctions, and the Strait of Hormuz will be reopened. A $300 billion plan for Iran's reconstruction is also included. The agreement paves the way for further talks to resolve outstanding issues, primarily the future of Iran's nuclear program. Over the next 60 days, both sides will continue negotiating to reach a final agreement. The deal marks a significant diplomatic breakthrough, with the potential to ease tensions between the two nations and have far-reaching implications for the region. US and Iranian officials will work to finalize the agreement within the agreed timeframe.

stories.headline: As Australia prepares for Modi's visit, what’s next for this strategic partnership?
stories.summary: Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong visited Delhi, reaffirming the growing strength of India-Australia relations after talks with Indian officials. The countries are enhancing their Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, focusing on areas such as defense, trade, technology, and supply chain resilience. India's Defense Minister Rajnath Singh recently visited Canberra, marking the first such trip and underscoring Australia's goal of seeing India as an "indispensable security partner." Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi has expressed aspirations to achieve new heights in collaboration with Australia through their partnership. The strengthening of ties comes ahead of Modi's upcoming visit to Australia, expected to further solidify the strategic partnership between the two nations in key sectors. Discussions have emphasized the importance of cooperation in defense, trade, and technology to ensure mutual benefit and regional stability.

stories.headline: Materials Shares Edge Up as Geopolitics Weigh on Global Supplies -- Materials Roundup
stories.summary: Materials shares have edged up as geopolitical tensions impact global supply chains. The US-Iran talks are being closely watched to see if they can help normalize supplies. Prices of key commodities such as gold, copper, and aluminum have been affected by the uncertainty. Global trade reached a record $35 trillion in 2025 and is expected to continue growing in 2026, but fragility is rising due to geopolitical competition. Investors are weighing the impact of inflation pressures and the Federal Reserve's next move on the materials sector. As a result, shares of materials companies have posted modest gains, reflecting the complex interplay of global events and economic factors influencing the industry. The situation remains volatile, with markets closely monitoring developments that could further disrupt or stabilize global supply chains.

stories.headline: Who is Parimal Nathwani, the four-time Rajya Sabha MP who rattled INDIA bloc in Jharkhand?
stories.summary: NDA-backed Independent candidate Parimal Nathwani won a Rajya Sabha seat from Jharkhand, despite the NDA lacking the numbers in the 81-member Assembly. This suggests suspected cross-voting by allies of the INDIA bloc, dealing a blow to Congress candidate Pranav Jha. Nathwani secured victory, marking his fourth term as a Rajya Sabha MP and third stint representing Jharkhand. He had earlier represented the state from 2008 to 2020 and also served a term from Andhra Pradesh. The win has triggered unease in the INDIA bloc, with at least five votes from rivals reportedly going to Nathwani. The outcome has exposed cracks within the bloc, with the second Rajya Sabha seat from Jharkhand going to another candidate. Nathwani's victory is seen as a significant outcome of the June 18 Rajya Sabha elections.

stories.headline: No other headlines were provided to select from, please provide more headlines for a comprehensive selection.
stories.summary: Australian Federal Police arrested two Sydney residents after discovering a large quantity of drugs buried in bunkers beneath shipping containers. The drugs were found in plastic tubs on June 19 in western Sydney. Meanwhile, in other news, Lionel Messi became the top scorer in World Cup history with two more goals for Argentina. In separate incidents, a report on a 2025 flash flood at a Texas summer camp revealed inadequate emergency plans and staff training, and authorities are investigating ransom notes sent to the family of an abducted person. Additionally, a bipartisan US housing bill aims to prevent major investors from hoarding homes, and a beverage company is using QR codes to provide nutritional information on over 140 ingredients. These developments highlight various global events and issues, including crime, sports, and social topics.

stories.summary: NPR provides comprehensive coverage of national and world news, including politics, business, science, and technology. The platform offers breaking stories, in-depth analysis, and extended coverage of major events. Users can access a wide range of news sources, including audio and podcasts, as well as a daily updated free press review of newspaper front pages from around the world. The NPR Nation RSS feed allows subscribers to stay informed about the latest developments in U.S. politics, elections, arts, culture, health, and science. With continuous updates from top local, regional, national, and international online news sources, NPR offers a one-stop destination for news enthusiasts. Google News aggregates news from sources worldwide, providing users with a broad perspective on current events. Overall, NPR's coverage is diverse, up-to-date, and easily accessible.

stories.headline: Sensex, Nifty drop over 1% as global cues, FII outflows trigger market tailspin
stories.summary: Stock market benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty dropped over 1% due to negative global cues and fresh foreign fund outflows. Weakness in HDFC Bank and IT firms also contributed to the decline. The Indian equity markets have been experiencing a downturn, with foreign institutional investor (FII) outflows and global market trends weighing heavily on investor sentiment. This trend has been ongoing for weeks, with the NIFTY50 and BSE SENSEX indices previously tumbling more than 1% on June 8, influenced by global market cues and oil prices. The current market situation is characterized by weak trading in equities, with fresh outflows of foreign funds exacerbating the decline. The ongoing weakness in key sectors and global market uncertainty continue to impact the Indian stock market.

stories.headline: Stock markets go into tailspin; Sensex, Nifty drop over 1%
stories.summary: Indian stock markets faced heavy selling pressure on Tuesday, with benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty dropping over 1% each. The BSE Sensex tanked 893.39 points to 76,200.68, while the NSE Nifty fell 278.80 points to 23,824.10. The decline was attributed to a bearish trend in global markets, weakness in HDFC Bank and IT firms, and foreign fund outflows. Rising Iran-US tensions, persistent FII selling, and a surge in oil prices also contributed to the broad-based selloff. The market capitalization lost over Rs 3 lakh crore due to the decline. The selling pressure was widespread, with various sectors experiencing losses, leading to a significant drop in the stock market indices. The decline is a continuation of the bearish trend seen in global markets, affecting investor sentiment in India.

stories.headline: Sensex trades on choppy note, Nifty below 24,100 as IT stocks drag benchmarks lower
stories.summary: Indian stock markets are trading on a choppy note, with the Sensex down and the Nifty below 24,100. IT stocks are weighing down the benchmarks, causing them to decline. Earlier, the Sensex had dropped over 250 points in the opening session, and the Nifty had fallen below 23,824. The Indian equities extended losses, with the Sensex declining by 533 points and the Nifty dropping 167 points. However, the Nifty had closed above 24,100 in a previous session, with stocks like Tech Mahindra and Sun Pharma among the gainers. The current market trend is volatile, with the Sensex and Nifty experiencing significant fluctuations in recent sessions. The benchmarks are now trading lower, with the Sensex at 77,050 and the Nifty below 24,100, indicating a bearish trend in the Indian stock market.

stories.headline: Stock Market Today: Sensex Falls 70 Points, Nifty Slips To 24,089 As IT Stocks Drag
stories.summary: The Indian stock market fell on June 23, with the BSE Sensex declining 70 points to 77,024 and the NSE Nifty 50 slipping 14 points to 24,089. IT and metal stocks were major laggards, contributing to the market decline. The fall was attributed to escalating Middle East tensions, a surge in crude oil prices, and concerns over inflation. Additionally, IT stocks faced pressure after Accenture's sell-off. The Sensex dropped nearly 1,000 points, or 1.28%, to 76,200, while the Nifty50 declined about 280 points, or 1.16%, to 23,824. Major losers included Infosys, TCS, Tata Steel, BEL, and Adani Ports, falling as much as 3.5% in afternoon trade. The market decline was also mirrored in Asian peers, with negative sentiment prevailing due to potential delays in Fed rate cuts.

stories.headline: SA government moves to regulate AI data centres as water, energy concerns mount
stories.summary: The South Australian government is drafting legislation to regulate the development of AI data centres due to concerns over water and energy usage. The move aims to streamline data centre development while ensuring sustainable water use and managing energy needs to avoid pressure on bills. Local farmers and residents have raised concerns about the project's impact on national security and the environment. The government is working with companies to develop a framework for managing large-scale data centre proposals. Experts suggest implementing technologies like air cooling to reduce water usage, but note that current regulations do not mandate best practices. The legislation aims to address these concerns and provide a framework for responsible data centre development in the state. The government's plan comes amid a surge in clean energy projects and growing demand for data centre infrastructure.

stories.headline: Company controlled by Indonesian instant noodles tycoon Anthoni Salim to raise $396M from Philippine IPO
stories.summary: A company controlled by Indonesian billionaire Anthoni Salim is set to raise 24 billion pesos ($396 million) through an initial public offering (IPO) in the Philippines. The company, PLDT, is backed by Salim's Hong Kong-listed First Pacific Co. and will be the country's first real estate investment trust (REIT) focused exclusively on data centers. Anthoni Salim is the CEO of Indofood, one of the world's largest makers of instant noodles, and heads the Salim Group, which has investments in food, retail, banking, telecom, and energy. The IPO marks a significant milestone for the Philippine market and is expected to be a major development in the country's data center industry. Salim's business empire includes various listed companies on the Indonesian Stock Exchange (BEI).

stories.headline: Avolta to acquire DFS Okinawa, marking Japanese travel retail market debut
stories.summary: Avolta has entered into an agreement to acquire 100% of DFS Okinawa, a duty-free and airport retail business on the Japanese island of Okinawa. The transaction marks Avolta's entry into the Japanese travel retail market, providing immediate scale in the country through airport and downtown retail operations. This acquisition strengthens Avolta's presence in Asia Pacific, a key region for the company. The move allows Avolta to deepen its Asian footprint, securing a new platform in travel retail. The acquisition is a significant development for Avolta, enabling the company to expand its operations in one of Asia's most dynamic travel retail markets. The deal is expected to enhance Avolta's position in the region, with Okinawa serving as a strategic location for the company's growth in Japan.

stories.headline: ANZ cuts home loan and term deposit rates after fall in wholesale costs
stories.summary: ANZ has cut its fixed home loan and term deposit rates, following a decrease in wholesale costs. The bank's 2- and 3-year fixed home loan rates have been reduced by up to 0.10 percentage points, with its lowest fixed rate now at 6.29% for a 2-year term. This move comes after the Reserve Bank's 0.5% official cash rate (OCR) cut. ANZ's one-year home loan special rate has fallen by 2.6% and its one-year term deposit rate has dropped by 2.4% since March 2024. Infometrics chief executive Brad Olsen expects other lenders to match ANZ's rates within the next week, suggesting ANZ is getting ahead of the next OCR decision. The rate cuts aim to keep ANZ's interest rates competitive, with other banks likely to follow suit.

stories.headline: Getty Images surges 145% after announcing OpenAI deal
stories.summary: Getty Images Holdings Inc. shares surged as much as 145% after announcing a licensing deal with OpenAI. The partnership allows Getty's licensed content libraries to appear across OpenAI search and discovery experiences within ChatGPT. Financial terms of the agreement were not disclosed, and it is unclear whether Getty's library will be used to train future models. The multi-year display agreement enables Getty Images' content to be featured inside ChatGPT search experiences. The significant increase in Getty Images' stock price followed the announcement, with shares jumping intraday. The deal marks a notable collaboration between Getty Images and OpenAI, expanding the visibility of Getty's image library through ChatGPT's search and discovery features. Getty Images' stock closed up significantly after the announcement, reflecting the market's positive response to the partnership.

stories.headline: SpaceX’s Explosive Debut Proves Investors Are Hungry for OpenAI and Anthropic IPOs
stories.summary: SpaceX's initial public offering (IPO) has seen a strong debut, with shares climbing over 37% in its first week as a public company. This rally has fueled interest in upcoming IPOs from similar companies, including OpenAI and Anthropic. The three companies are expected to collectively raise $200 billion and add $4 trillion to the American stock market capitalization. SpaceX's IPO is particularly notable, as it is the largest-ever initial public offering. OpenAI and Anthropic are also gearing up for highly anticipated IPOs, with investors showing significant interest. The success of SpaceX's IPO has demonstrated investor appetite for these types of companies, setting the stage for potential future growth and investment opportunities in the tech industry. The upcoming IPOs are expected to be closely watched by investors and industry analysts.

stories.headline: Google takes the hit in AI's talent war
stories.summary: Google is facing setbacks in the AI talent war, with two high-profile researchers leaving Google DeepMind in a single week. This marks a significant loss for the company, which is competing with other tech giants to attract and retain top AI talent. The departures are part of a larger trend of high-profile moves in the AI industry, with several major labs experiencing a flurry of exits. As a result, Alphabet Inc.'s shares, Google's parent company, tumbled in morning trade. The AI talent war is intensifying, with companies shelling out top dollar to lure top talent, and Google is taking a hit in the battle for stars. The recent departures have upped the ante in the competition for AI talent, making it challenging for Google to achieve its AI ambitions.

stories.headline: Alphabet Shares Fall As AI Talent Departures And Competitive Concerns Weigh On Investors
stories.summary: Alphabet's stock suffered its biggest one-day decline in over a year, falling 5.5-7% on Monday, due to concerns over the company's loss of artificial intelligence talent. Noam Shazeer, Google DeepMind's vice president of engineering and co-lead of the Gemini AI models, has left to join OpenAI, raising concerns about a brain drain at the heart of Alphabet's AI ambitions. Another senior AI researcher also departed, fueling worries about competition in the industry. Investors are questioning whether Alphabet's heavy AI spending can deliver a durable competitive edge, leading to a record loss of market capitalization. The departures and rising competition concerns have sparked a selloff, with Alphabet's stock tracking for its worst daily drop in about a year. The decline reflects investor concerns over the company's ability to retain top talent and maintain its position in the AI sector.
